summary: Petition seeking to surrender Category V Trading Licence in terms of Regulation 20(3) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading license and other related matters) Regulations, 2020. **Parties present:** Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Advocate, SEL Ms. Aishwarya Subramani, Advocate, SEL Ms. Harsha V. Rao, Advocate, SEL 4. The Applicant has submitted that there are no outstanding liabilities in respect of its inter-State trading licence and that no claim has been raised by any party since 1.4.2026. It is further stated that no operative contract is pending against the licensee and that the licence fee for the Financial Year 2026-27 has been duly paid. The Applicant has prayed for relaxation in respect of payment of the annual licence fee for the period from 1.4.2026 to 31.3.2027. 5. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Applicant reiterated the submissions made in the Application and further submitted that the Applicant has published a notice in relation to the present Application and sought time to place the same on record, i.e., the details of such publication. Learned counsel further submitted that the Petitioner has already paid the annual licence fee up to the financial year 2026-27. 6. Vide the Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as “RoP”) for the hearing dated 4.8.2026, the Application was admitted and the Applicant was directed to submit, on an affidavit, the information and clarifications regarding compliance with the requirements stipulated under Regulation 20(3)(c) and (d) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, along with a declaration that no obligation remains outstanding on the part of the Applicant towards the Haryana Power Purchase Centre (or any other entities), as was brought to the notice of the Commission in Petition No. 277/MP/2022. 7. In compliance with the Record of Proceedings dated 4.8.2026, the Applicant, vide affidavit dated 21.8.2026, has submitted that it had published the notice of its Application along with annexures and enclosures on its website and in the newspapers, namely Business Standard and Mint, on 15.7.2026. The Applicant further submitted that no obligation is outstanding towards the Haryana Power Purchase Centre or any other entity, as was brought to the Commission’s notice in Petition No. 277/MP/2022. 8. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that the directions issued vide RoP dated 4.8.2026 had been complied with and that an affidavit in compliance thereof had been placed on record. Learned counsel accordingly prayed that the matter be reserved for orders. After hearing the learned counsel for the _(3) Where the Trading Licensee makes an application for revocation of licence, the application shall contain the following information and documents: (a) reasons for seeking revocation;_ _(b) an affidavit to the effect that the Trading Licensee has deposited the licence fee for the Year in which revocation is sought; that there are no undischarged liabilities against the Trading Licensee; and that there are no operative contracts for trading of electricity to which the applicant is a party at the time of filing the said application;_ _(c) an affidavit to the effect that the applicant has posted the complete application on its website and shall keep the application uploaded on its website till its disposal by the Commission;_ _(d) documents showing that the Trading Licensee has published the notice about its application for revocation in two daily newspapers having circulation in each of the five regions in addition to those published from Delhi including one economic newspaper.”_ published the notices regarding the surrender of the inter-State trading licence on 15.7.2026 in all editions of Business Standard and Mint. However, the Applicant has received no comments/ objections from the general public. 12. With respect to the relaxation sought by the Applicant in terms of the payment of annual fees for 1.4.2026 to 31.3.2027 under Regulation 23 of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, we note that the present Petition was filed by the Applicant on 26.6.2026, which is well after the commencement of the Financial Year 2026-27. It is pertinent to note that the Commission, vide Order dated 28.4.2026 in Petition No. 7/SM/2026, had initiated Suo-motu proceedings against the Applicant for willful default in depositing the annual licence fee for the preceding two financial years (2024-25 and 2025-26), as well as for failure to undertake any trading activity and submit requisite information. The instant Petition for surrender of Inter-State trading licence was filed subsequent to the issuance of the said _Suo-motu_ notice. By retaining the Category ‘V’ trading licence and failing to file the surrender Petition prior to the commencement of Financial Year 2026-27, the Applicant remained a licensee in the records of the Commission and was obligated to pay the annual licence fee for Financial Year 202627, which was required to be paid till 30.4.2026. The Applicant has deposited the fee for the said financial year, seemingly to rectify its defaults and comply with its statutory obligations in light of the Suo-motu proceedings. In view of the Applicant's delay in filing the surrender Petition, its prior track record of fee defaults that necessitated the Suo-motu intervention, the prayer of the Applicant for relaxation under Regulation 23 from the payment of the annual licence fee for the period 1.04.2026 to 31.3.2027 is not allowed. 14. Let a copy of this order be sent to the Central Government in the Ministry of Power and the CEA for their information and record.
title: Petition seeking to surrender Category V Trading Licence in terms of Regulation 20(3) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading license and other related matters) Regulations, 2020. Svaryu Energy Limited
